I've been disappointed by similar products before, so quality really matters to me.

I hear you. When you’ve been let down before, it’s hard to trust the next purchase, especially with plants that you’re investing time, money, and care into.

A few things about Heirloom that might help ease your mind:

We grow our own roses at our nurseries in Oregon and sell them as premium, own-root plants in 1-gallon containers with soil (not bare root from third-party suppliers). This gives us a lot of control over quality.
Our plants are selected and grown to be vigorous and true to variety, and we defoliate roses before shipping so they travel better and can focus on root growth once you plant them.
Roses are covered by a one-year guarantee, perennials by a 90-day guarantee, and bulbs by a failure-to-bloom guarantee. If something doesn’t perform as expected, our garden advisors review it and work with you.

I’d love to match you with something that really fits, not just “something pretty.” To do that well, can you tell me:

Are you looking for a rose, another perennial (like lavender, hydrangea, etc.), or bulbs?
Your ZIP code or hardiness zone, so I only suggest things that are actually suitable for your climate.
What matters most to you this time: fragrance, big blooms, strong disease resistance, low maintenance, something for cutting, or something to cover a fence/arch?

Once I have those details, I can narrow it down to a few specific choices and explain why they’re good fits, so you’re not repeating a disappointing experience.
